units.title: Build the missing rank-one covariance
units.boundary: An explicit covariance producer, not the whole Gaussian absorption lemma. Principal matrix-square-root identification, scaling, block seed law and physical-query translation remain separate.

sources.label: Pinned OAI compiler absorption: covariance identity
sources.scope: Authored generic prerequisite for the slot-space matrix square root. This statement does not assert the source's complete output-law lemma.

assumptions: E is a complete real inner-product space; finite-dimensional real source slot spaces satisfy completeness automatically.
u is a vector with ||u||<=1. In the paper u=v/(2Ds), and source assumptions give the stronger bound ||u||<=1/2.
No square-root witness, covariance identity, Gaussian law, invertibility or nonzero-vector assumption is supplied.
units.statement: Let E be a complete real inner-product space and let u in E satisfy ||u||<=1. There exists a continuous real-linear operator P:E->E that is positive (self-adjoint with nonnegative quadratic form) and satisfies P*P+u u*=I, where u u* sends x to <u,x>u. Zero vectors and the singular unit-norm boundary are included; finite dimension is not required.

steps.title: Choose a construction that also works at zero
steps.text: Set a to the nonnegative square root of 1 minus the squared norm of u. The coefficient c divides by 1+a, which is at least one, so there is no special division-by-zero branch. Define P by subtracting c times the rank-one operator from the identity.
steps.lean: Local a,c,P are literal constructions. hn justifies squaring the real square root; hden proves that the denominator is genuinely positive.

steps.title: Get the exact scalar cancellation
steps.text: The square-root identity implies the cancellation that will restore the missing rank-one covariance. This is an equality, without dimension factors or approximation slack. Also c lies between zero and one.
steps.lean: ha2 and hc identify the squared root and coefficient. Field arithmetic uses a nonzero denominator, rather than relying on totalized division.

steps.title: Verify positivity, not only a formal square
steps.text: The rank-one operator is self-adjoint. Cauchy–Schwarz and the bound on u give squared inner product at most squared norm of x. Since c is nonnegative and at most one, subtracting that rank-one quadratic term leaves a nonnegative quadratic form.
steps.lean: adjoint_rankOne supplies self-adjointness. isPositive_iff' requires the genuine self-adjoint and nonnegative quadratic-form conditions; hib and hci discharge the latter.

steps.title: Multiply the operators and restore covariance
steps.text: The square of the rank-one operator is its squared vector norm times itself. Expand P squared and insert the exact coefficient cancellation. This constructs the covariance condition that a Gaussian-law consumer needs, instead of taking that condition as an unproved input.
steps.lean: The proof checks operator equality pointwise using rankOne_apply and inner-product linearity. The concluding module calculation uses hc. No covariance premise is added.

units.lean_statement: IsPositive means self-adjointness and a nonnegative quadratic form. .adjoint.comp is composition with the Hilbert adjoint; rankOne is x mapped to <u,x>u. The existential P is proved by construction, not a hypothesis or a source-level algorithm.
units.lean_proof: The proof follows construction, exact scalar cancellation, positivity and covariance multiplication. This route avoids selecting an arbitrary matrix basis and does not require a real continuous-functional-calculus typeclass.
